questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Ukraine?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Ukraine article.

questions.proof: Its capital and largest city is Kyiv.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Ukraine?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Ukraine on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Ukraine article.

questions.proof: It borders Russia, Belarus, Poland, Slovakia, Hungary, Romania, and Moldova.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Kyiv?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Ukraine is Kyiv.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Ukraine on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Ukraine on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Ukraine about 603,550 square kilometres; Japan about 377,974 square kilometres; Qatar about 11,437 square kilometres; Luxembourg about 2,593 square kilometres.
